summary.text: James Mol is the Democratic candidate for the Connecticut House of Representatives, District 61, in the November 3, 2026 general election against incumbent Tami Zawistowski (R / Independent Party of Connecticut).

In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a small-business owner and farmer who has served on the Suffield Board of Education since 2019 and said he is running to address education funding and property taxes.

paragraphs.text: In a Ballotpedia survey, Mol said he runs a small hospitality consulting business, has three children in Suffield's public schools and has served on the Suffield Board of Education since 2019, including its Finance and Facilities Subcommittee.
He said that he and his wife bought a farm in West Suffield in 2008 to keep it from being developed.
Mol said he is running to bring his school-budget experience to Suffield, East Granby and Windsor Locks.

His stated priorities include a modernized, inflation-indexed education funding formula written into permanent law, full funding of the 2025 special education grant, and a funding formula in which household income counts for more than property value alone.
He also named farmland preservation and farming viability, road safety, and the benefits of Bradley International Airport to the surrounding towns as areas of focus.
Mol said he was endorsed by the Democratic Party at the 61st District nominating convention, AFSCME Council 4 and AFT Connecticut.
